findings.failureScenario: The Node package documents browser and QA tooling with no Rust pair, while rightkit-qa claims to replace @rightkit/qa. Their surfaces differ: Node exports browser/CDP, loopback, process, storage, evidence, and guards; Rust targets native app/control scenarios with optional Chrome. An owner or consumer can therefore infer a migration or select a harness without a current API and platform contract.
findings.action: Reconcile one current ownership statement, publish an API/platform matrix, and add concrete same-host consumer evidence before any migration. Keep Node/browser and Rust desktop runners separate until that evidence exists; share only a versioned evidence or receipt contract if needed.

findings.failureScenario: rightkit-qts-ggml remains a published compatibility facade whose manifest and crate docs direct consumers to rightkit-qts-ggml-sys, while rightkit-qts already depends on the sys crate directly. New code can still choose the deprecated layer, preserving an unnecessary public boundary and maintenance path.
findings.action: Keep the facade compatibility-only with no new API. Confirm zero in-tree dependants, communicate the direct sys-crate replacement, and retire the wrapper on the next breaking release after external-consumer review.

findings.failureScenario: rightkit-send persists trust records through a private write_atomic helper that creates parents, sets Unix mode 0600, syncs only the file, renames, and cleans failed temps. rightkit-fs owns a broader atomic writer with private-directory policy, no-follow temp creation, existing-mode handling, replacement and retry options, and directory fsync. Replacing the send helper without checking these semantics could change trust-store durability, permissions, symlink behavior, or Windows results.
findings.action: Review trust-store persistence against rightkit-fs for directory durability, owner-only results, Windows behavior, symlink and mode handling, and failure cleanup. Then delegate with matching options or record a protocol-specific exception.
